_note: Boxes are NORMALISED to the tile (0-1). THE BOTTOM-RIGHT CORNER OF THE SCROLL -- its right edge IS the painting's right edge and its bottom edge IS the painting's bottom edge. Overlaps t006 by 77% (shifted right by 0.234 of a tile width), so the grove, the two trunks and the root mass are the same objects seen again; the genuinely new content is the right-hand strip x > 0.77. MIXED, split the same way as t006: canopy above y 0.30, bare rock and root below. New in this tile: a solid black-ink PINNATE-leaf tree at the top right (a different species from the blue-green 夾葉 grove), a blue-green orchid tuft on the right bank, two large red collector seals, and two ink inscription characters at the extreme right edge. The pink/ochre stroke-fans at y 0.28-0.40 are 牛毛皴 texture on rock, NOT autumn foliage -- same verdict as t006, checked at 4x.

objects.name: left crown of double-outline oval leaves, clipped by the left edge
objects.note: same crown as t006's canopy-upper-left, entering from the left. Dense 夾葉 with blue-green wash

objects.name: faded creeper strands with hanging leaf sprays, left edge
objects.note: the right tail of t006's vine curtain, much more worn here -- pale grey-green sprays on threads over pale rock. Faint enough that a contrast-based mask will drop it entirely. Sparse by nature: mask from the leaf glyphs, never fill the box

objects.name: central crown between the two trunks
objects.note: = t006's canopy-centre. Densest blue-green mass in the tile; a pink rock face shows through a gap near [0.33,0.14,0.40,0.20], so the box is not solid

objects.name: right crown around and behind the main trunk
objects.note: = t006's canopy-right. Leaf tongues cross in front of the main trunk at x 0.52-0.58 -- leaves move, bark does not

objects.name: solid black-ink lanceolate leaf cluster inside the right crown
objects.note: = t006's dark-leaf-cluster-right. Filled black strokes, no outline, no wash. Reads as a shadow at tile scale; it is foliage

objects.name: far-right crown running to the painting's right edge
objects.note: NEW CONTENT -- this strip is past t006's right edge. Blue-green 夾葉 continuing to x = 1.0, which is the physical edge of the silk. The leaf mass is cut by the edge, so any hinge here must be anchored inboard or the cut edge will visibly shear

objects.name: black-ink pinnate/feathery leaf sprays at the top right
objects.note: A THIRD SPECIES and the most distinctive foliage in either tile: solid black compound leaves with paired leaflets down a central rib, like a locust or fern frond. The upper red seal is stamped ON TOP of these leaves -- the seal is later ink on the surface, not something behind them, so a depth pass must not push it back. Do not let the seal's red bleed into the leaf mask

objects.name: lower spray of the same black pinnate leaves
objects.note: the same tree's lower frond, hanging clear of the crown against pale rock. Cleanest, best-separated leaf mass in the tile -- the easiest single subject here to animate correctly

objects.name: blue-green orchid-grass tuft on the right bank
objects.note: a fan of long arching blades, one stroke each, in clear blue-green -- the ONLY vegetation in the lower half of the right side and completely isolated on bare rock. Small, and exactly the kind of thing that gets skipped; if the grove above stirs and this does not, the eye lands on it

objects.name: tail of the bamboo clump, lower-left corner
objects.note: the right-hand blades of t006's bamboo-clump-lower-left, clipped by the left edge. Faded to grey-blue here. Must be driven by the SAME motion as the t006 clump or the seam will show as two bamboos out of phase

objects.name: left trunk with a heavy vine coiled around it
objects.note: = t006's trunk-vine-wrapped. The coiled liana is woody structure, not a leafy vine. Rigid

objects.name: the great knotted trunk, centre
objects.note: = t006's main-trunk, seen more fully here: it runs unbroken from the top edge down to y 0.63 where it flares into the root mass. Burl knots and hollow eyes. The single most important thing to keep OUT of the foliage mask

objects.name: the mass of exposed looping roots across the bank
objects.note: tan rope-like roots with double contours coiling over the rock. Structurally trunk, rigid either way. Visually restless -- an automatic motion pass will want to move it; it must not

objects.name: band of rounded boulders under the canopy
objects.note: THE TRAP. Fans of fine tapered parallel strokes under a warm pink/ochre wash, which read as hanging autumn leaves at tile scale. At 4x every stroke follows the dome of the stone and terminates on its contour line, and there is no green in the passage anywhere -- 牛毛皴 hemp-fibre texture, i.e. rock. A warm-tone colour threshold will grab this and animate stone, which is precisely the failure that got the earlier pass rejected

objects.name: pale rock shelf down the right side
objects.note: sparse dry-brush 皴 over light ochre. The orchid tuft grows out of its lower edge; nothing else here moves

objects.name: the broad foreground bank filling the bottom
objects.note: long sweeping contours, darkening into wet-ink boulders below y 0.82. This is the bottom edge of the painting -- no water, no vegetation, no figures. Plainly and entirely rock

objects.name: large red collector seal at the top right
objects.note: stamped over the black pinnate foliage. Later ink on the surface of the silk: it must stay perfectly rigid and perfectly flat while the leaves under it move, or the whole illusion breaks. Never include it in a foliage mask on the strength of its saturation

objects.name: large red collector seal on the lower-right bank
objects.note: stamped on bare rock, well clear of everything. Rigid

objects.name: ink character 聖 at the right edge
objects.note: a single brushed character, part of a vertical inscription column that continues off the right edge of the silk. Not painting content -- rigid, and it must not be treated as a dark leaf glyph

objects.name: ink character at the right edge, lower
objects.note: second character of the same edge inscription, half cut by the silk edge. Rigid
